history: Support sees a steady trickle of 'where is my project plan?' tickets in each account's first week. Product wants to move the timeline entry point into the left navigation; design believes new users look in the header toolbar first. Leadership decides at the January planning review with no evidence in hand.
decision: Do we ship the left-navigation timeline entry or invest in a guided tour? Owner: Product Leadership, January planning review.

hypotheses.label: H1
hypotheses.text: First-week users look for planning features in the header toolbar before the left navigation.

hypotheses.label: H2
hypotheses.text: New project managers who find the timeline in their first session build a plan in that session.

hypotheses.label: H3
hypotheses.text: A navigation change increases first-session timeline discovery more than a guided tour.

assumptions.label: A1
assumptions.text: First-week users want to build a plan during their first session.

research_questions: Where do first-week users look for the timeline when they want to plan?
What does a first-session planning attempt look like for a new project manager?
What makes the timeline entry discoverable in the left navigation vs the header toolbar?
persona: New project manager in their first week on a trial account
study_title: New user navigation study: timeline discoverability
